summary: Every accuracy and fairness item from round 3 has landed. I checked each one on the regenerated sheets (13:21-13:35 local, after the 14:28-15:03Z ledger records). Marcus card (ch09-s05): 'GARY MARCUS · 2018 · Deep Learning: A Critical Appraisal' is pinned from 22.0 through 23.21. Dreyfus quote card (ch05-s07): the verbatim q-dreyfus-pattern text, attributed '— Hubert Dreyfus, 1972', is on screen from 26.46 to 30.38, under a name card reading 'What Computers Can't Do, 1972'. LeCun / AMI Labs label (ch15-s06): it reads 'left Meta, Nov 2025, to build world models · AMI Labs' from 8.08 to the end and matches e14-lecun. The three ch14-s04b position tags now hang in one row at equal size: HELPS HUAWEI, then SELF-DEFEATING, then DECISIVE (12.42, 14.33). The settlement label (ch15-s05) carries the 'ANTHROPIC ·' prefix from 22.79. The plinths also carry GOOGLE DEEPMIND and META tags (film frame at 33:13.6). L1405 now says 'a year or two behind' [e13-gap] in script, timeline and VTT, and so do the candle labels in ch14-s02, ch14-s04b and the ch15-s04 shelf. A grep of the shot sources finds no remaining 'one to three'. A fresh machine check found 0 mismatches between quotes.json and every narrated or on-screen quotation. Script text equals timeline.json for all 233 lines. Every cited claim id exists, and every claim marked contested is framed in the film as contested. The FTX caveat, the paired Lin and Katsas quotes, the MacroPolo halves, the authorship disclosure and the live sources URL all survived the round-3 re-cuts. What remains is small: (1) L1410b's callback 'China trailing by years?' no longer matches the revised candle 'a year or two behind'; (2) the narrator's pronunciation of real names (Amodei, LeCun, Uszkoreit, Hochreiter, Schmidhuber, Rumelhart, Lenat) still awaits human sign-off; (3) L0114's take runs at 221 wpm, against the user's recorded direction 'at normal pace'; (4) two ledger partials (ch15-s08 stamp foley, ch13-s01 Hinton hair) need closing; ch15-s05's partial is resolved by the ruling below.
